provenance.derivation: Every expected answer below restates a fact the owner recorded in that review. Nothing was inferred from ARKitScenes annotation boxes, from Mask3D output, from learned labels, or from any run artifact.
provenance.why_a_separate_file: The review declares itself 'partial_visual_review_not_a_qa_key'. This file is the key; it does not modify or replace the review, and the review remains the sole source of its content.
provenance.independence: Questions are phrased about the SCENE, never about a delivered instance id. A system is scored on what it reports about the room, so the key stays valid across perception changes.
provenance.authored_before_scoring: This key was written and hashed before any system answer was read.

scoring_rules.count_source: instances carrying an admitted display label equal to the class, after the label stage's own admission threshold; unlabelled instances are not counted
scoring_rules.class_normalization: the graph's canonical hyphen form; underscore and space variants map to the same class family
scoring_rules.unanswerable: If the system emits no relation of the required type at all, the item is scored `unanswered` and reported separately from `wrong`. A system that cannot express an answer has not given a wrong one.
scoring_rules.partial_credit: none; each item is correct, wrong, or unanswered

independent_questions.question: How many rugs are in this scene?
independent_questions.review_basis: the scene contains one rug, not the many rugs suggested by learned labels

independent_questions.question: How many trash cans are in this scene?
independent_questions.review_basis: the scene contains one trash can

independent_questions.question: How many kitchen counters are in this scene?
independent_questions.review_basis: there is one main kitchen counter

independent_questions.question: Is there a sofa or couch in this scene?
independent_questions.review_basis: sofa cushions rest on the sofa/couch (the review's own diagnosis also corrects obj_13 to sofa)

independent_questions.question: Are there cushions in this scene?
independent_questions.review_basis: sofa cushions rest on the sofa/couch
independent_questions.note: Presence only. The review says 'cushions' and separately diagnoses two instances, but never states the cushion count as a scene fact, so no cardinality item is asserted here.

independent_questions.question: What do the sofa cushions rest on?
independent_questions.review_basis: sofa cushions rest on the sofa/couch

independent_questions.question: Is the kitchen counter a room-spanning planar region?
independent_questions.expected_detail: No instance reported as the kitchen counter should span the room. The owner reports the counter is a bounded object.
independent_questions.review_basis: the delivered whole-plane region labeled counter is not the counter object; recorded extent 7.38 x 5.95 x 0.20 m
independent_questions.scoring: Correct when every instance labelled `counter` has a horizontal footprint smaller than ROOM_SPAN_FRACTION of the scene footprint. This phrasing avoids naming obj_8, so the item survives a perception change.

unresolved_uid_mappings.why: The review confirms exactly one rug exists but does not say which delivered instance it is; obj_9 and obj_23 carry the learned label `rug` and were both diagnosed as cushions.
unresolved_uid_mappings.needed_from_owner: the delivered uid of the one real rug, or a statement that none of the delivered instances is it
unresolved_uid_mappings.blocks: any per-instance rug scoring; q1 counts only, and does not check identity

unresolved_uid_mappings.why: The review confirms one trash can and corrects obj_36 from `trash-can` to `cabinet`, leaving the real one unassigned.
unresolved_uid_mappings.needed_from_owner: the delivered uid of the real trash can, or a statement that it was not delivered
unresolved_uid_mappings.blocks: per-instance trash-can scoring; q2 counts only

unresolved_uid_mappings.why: The review states obj_8 is an overmerged whole-plane region and NOT the counter, leaving the counter unassigned.
unresolved_uid_mappings.needed_from_owner: the delivered uid of the main kitchen counter, or a statement that it was not delivered as a separate instance
unresolved_uid_mappings.blocks: per-instance counter scoring; q3 counts and q7 checks extent only

unresolved_uid_mappings.why: The review diagnoses obj_9 and obj_23 as cushions but never states how many cushions the scene contains.
unresolved_uid_mappings.needed_from_owner: the number of cushions, if a cardinality item is wanted
unresolved_uid_mappings.blocks: any cushion cardinality question; q5 asserts presence only

deliberately_excluded.item: per-instance label corrections (obj_13 sofa, obj_9/obj_23 cushion, obj_36 cabinet)
deliberately_excluded.why: These reference delivered instance ids, so a key built on them would be re-scoring the system against itself and would break the moment segmentation changes. The scene-level facts they imply are captured by q4, q5 and q6.
Different scene. The curtains fact belongs to that scene's review.

deliberately_excluded.item: counts of any class the review does not state
deliberately_excluded.why: The review is a partial visual review. Absence of a statement is not a statement of absence, and inventing counts would manufacture ground truth.

interpretation_limit: Seven items from one partial visual review of one scene. This is a human scene-fact key, not a benchmark, and a score against it is not an end-to-end QA result.

known_confounds.description: If the system labels the sofa as a cushion, q5 passes and q4 fails for one and the same error. q5 must not then be read as evidence the system found the cushions.
known_confounds.detection: q4 wrong AND q5 correct is the signature; the scorer flags it automatically.
known_confounds.review_basis: the review diagnoses obj_13 as the sofa, and rgb_tight labels obj_13 `cushion`. That per-instance fact is deliberately outside the key, so the confound is recorded here rather than scored.
